title: Swift Regex: Extract Dates
hints: Regex literals like `/(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})/` have typed captures.
Use `matches(of:)`, destructure `match.output`, and check the month and day ranges numerically.
`let (_, year, month, day) = match.output` then return `"\(day)/\(month)/\(year)"`.
jsBridge: Swift regex literals (`/(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})/`) are compile-time checked and **typed**: captures become a tuple of `Substring`s. JS regexes give untyped `string[]` matches.

compass.q: JS `match[1]` is `string | undefined`. What does a typed Swift capture tuple give you?
Why validate month/day numerically after matching instead of in the regex?
Regex literal vs `NSRegularExpression` vs `RegexBuilder`: when would you use each?
Should an app parse dates with regex at all? What does `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle` give you?
